title: Crocodile stitch — the overlapping scale
subtitle: Five trebles worked around each side of a V-stitch frame to build up overlapping scales
excerpt: Crocodile stitch builds overlapping scales onto a V-stitch framework. Each scale is ten trebles — five worked down one post of a V-stitch and five worked up the other — forming a fan that folds over to look like a crocodile or fish scale. The effect is dramatic and three-dimensional.

glossaryTerms.definition: A three-dimensional crochet stitch where five trebles are worked around each arm of a V-stitch post in turn — five downward, five upward — to form a overlapping scale. Built onto a V-stitch skeleton framework.

heroPrompt: A crochet swatch in emerald green DK yarn showing four crocodile stitch scales, the overlapping 3D fan shapes clearly visible, close-up side-lit to show dimension.

content.text: is built in two passes. The first pass creates a skeleton of V-stitches (1 dc, ch 2, 1 dc into the same stitch), which become the frame for the scales. The second pass works five trebles around each arm of every V, creating a fan that folds over itself to produce the scale effect.
Foundation chain in a multiple of 6, plus 3. Row 1 (skeleton): ch 3. *Skip 2 ch. In next ch work (1 dc, ch 2, 1 dc) — one V. Ch 2. Skip 2 ch. Repeat from *.
Turn. Row 2: ch 3. *Work the V-stitch (1 dc, ch 2, 1 dc) into each ch-2 space of the V below. Ch 2 between each V. Repeat from *.
Work 5 tr down the left arm (post) of the first V-stitch — inserting around the post of each dc, not into the top.
Ch 2 at the bottom of the V (or sl st depending on pattern).
Work 5 tr up the right arm of the same V. The 10 trebles form a fan that curls over the ch-2 space of the V.
The scale flips over the V-frame. One scale complete. Continue to the next V.

items.symptom: Scale does not lie flat or fold over
items.cause: Too few trebles per arm, or trebles worked too tightly
items.fix: Each arm takes exactly 5 tr. Work them slightly loosely — tight trebles resist folding. If the scale still won't fold, add a sl st at the base of the V to pull it together before the 5-tr count begins.

content.text: Crocodile stitch worked in the round on a hat forms a full cover of scales without visible joining lines. Star stitch and spider stitch are similarly complex-looking stitches that become manageable once the repeating unit is understood.
